title: VP of Product Development

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Drytac's current overlaminating films (Weathershield series) offer 5-7 year outdoor durability, while Tedlar delivers 12-20+ years - a 2-3x performance advantage that represents a significant product differentiation opportunity. This role owns portfolio strategy and competitive positioning in a market where Drytac already competes on durability claims. The VP of Product Development would be directly responsible for evaluating next-generation film technologies that could: (1) enable premium product tier expansion with superior warranty offerings, (2) reduce warranty claim exposure from premature failures their current 5-7 year products may experience, (3) capitalize on their recent PRINTING United Pinnacle Award momentum by launching an industry-leading durability product, and (4) differentiate against commodity PVC competitors. Given Drytac's 50-year history and established R&D capabilities (UV stabilizers, anti-graffiti formulations), this role has both the technical sophistication to appreciate PVF chemistry advantages and the strategic mandate to explore materials that could redefine their competitive position in architectural graphics and vehicle wraps where longest lifecycle matters most.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: [Name] owns Drytac's product portfolio strategy, technical innovation roadmap, and competitive positioning for their overlaminating films and protective solutions. This role has direct authority over new material evaluations, product tier expansion decisions, and R&D investment priorities. They likely manage product engineers and collaborate closely with commercial teams to translate market needs into technical specifications. Given Drytac's 50-year legacy and recent award wins (PRINTING United Pinnacle Award for Interlam Eco Anti-Graffiti), [Name] operates with significant strategic influence and reports likely to C-suite or ownership. Their scope includes evaluating alternative chemistries (currently PVC-based) and determining whether to build, buy, or partner for next-generation solutions.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Drytac already competes in signs/graphics, vehicle wraps (Polar Grip Air), and anti-graffiti applications - making all Tedlar use cases directly relevant. Most compelling: (1) Architectural graphics for large-format building wraps where 12-20+ year performance justifies premium pricing and enables warranty expansion beyond their current 5-7 year Weathershield limits, (2) Vehicle wraps and fleet graphics where Tedlar's 2-3x longer lifespan reduces total ownership costs for corporate fleet customers who value ROI over decades, (3) Outdoor advertising and signage where UV resistance without yellowing/fading enables brands to maintain color integrity longer than competing PVC solutions, and (4) Transit interiors/exteriors where graffiti resistance (spray paint and marker removal) directly complements their existing anti-graffiti film portfolio. [Name]'s team would benefit by reducing warranty claim exposure, accessing premium market segments currently beyond Weathershield capabilities, and differentiating against commodity Asian PVC imports.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] likely owns KPIs including product line profitability, gross margin improvement, time-to-market for new solutions, warranty claim rates, and competitive win rates in premium segments. They personally care about solving: (1) commoditization pressure on existing PVC films where price competition erodes margins, (2) warranty exposure from 5-7 year products experiencing premature UV degradation or weathering failures, (3) inability to compete in ultra-premium architectural and transportation projects requiring 10+ year certifications, and (4) technical differentiation in a market where competitors offer similar PVC chemistry. Tedlar's 12-20+ year proven performance addresses all four: enables premium tier expansion with higher margins, reduces warranty risk through superior chemistry, opens addressable market in specification-driven projects, and provides defensible technical superiority. The UV resistance and graffiti-cleaning benefits directly reduce customer complaints and field failures that create internal pressure on product development.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Drytac exhibited at ISA Sign Expo 2025 (April 23-25, Mandalay Bay, Las Vegas) and PRINTING United Expo 2025 (October 22-24, Orlando) - making post-show periods ideal for technical discussions when [Name] is synthesizing customer feedback and competitive intelligence. Their recent PRINTING United Pinnacle Product Award for anti-graffiti film demonstrates active innovation momentum and receptivity to next-generation solutions. With 50 years in business and established global operations, they're positioned for portfolio evolution rather than early-stage experimentation. Current market pressures from Asian PVC imports and customer demands for longer warranties create urgency around identifying materials that can command premium pricing through provable performance advantages.

personalization_hooks.hook: Drytac's Weathershield films offer 5-7 year outdoor performance while Tedlar provides 12-20+ years - a 2-3x improvement that could redefine their premium product strategy
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging their strong position in protective films, then position Tedlar as the next evolution for customers who need warranties beyond what PVC chemistry can deliver. Frame as strategic partnership opportunity rather than competitive threat - their distribution and brand combined with Tedlar's chemistry.

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent PRINTING United Pinnacle Award for anti-graffiti innovation demonstrates commitment to solving customer pain points that Tedlar also addresses
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference their award-winning anti-graffiti work and position Tedlar as complementary - our graffiti resistance (spray paint/marker cleanup) combined with extreme UV protection creates a differentiated solution for transit, architectural, and outdoor advertising applications where both challenges exist simultaneously.

personalization_hooks.hook: Active presence at both ISA and PRINTING United expos indicates focus on architectural graphics and wide-format markets where lifecycle matters most to specifiers
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Mention their trade show leadership and suggest that customers in architectural/building wrap segments are increasingly specifying materials with 10+ year certifications - a space where Weathershield's 5-7 years falls short but Tedlar enables entry. Position as unlocking new revenue tiers in specification-driven projects.

recommended_approach: Lead with product portfolio expansion angle - acknowledge Drytac's strong market position and recent innovation awards, then frame Tedlar as enabling a premium tier above Weathershield that addresses the growing customer segment demanding 10+ year warranties. Use technical language (PVF chemistry, UV absorbers, proven field performance) to match [Name]'s sophistication. Avoid framing as competitive replacement; instead position as strategic addition that leverages their existing distribution and brand while accessing markets beyond PVC limitations. Request 20-minute technical discussion to explore fit.
